in_arabic.name: سامي
in_arabic.meaning: السامي: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي يعني العالي أو السامي
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم سامي مشتق من الفعل سامَ يَسمو إذا علا وارتفع، ومنه قوله تعالى: {وَيَسمو بَطَلاً مِنَ الأَرضِ لِأَعلى أَعلا العالَمينَ} أي عال ومرتفع. ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم كصفة لله تعالى، فهو السامي الذي علا وارتفع عن كل نقص أو عيب

in_hindi.name: सामी

data.cultural_impact: The name Sami is popular in both the Arab and Muslim communities, and is believed to represent peace and tranquility. This is in line with the Islamic value of promoting peace and harmony in both interpersonal relationships and within the broader society. The name can be given to both boys and girls and is a common choice for parents who wish to give their child a name that embodies peaceful and positive qualities.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic tradition, the name Sami is deeply rooted in spiritual significance. It is believed that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) once used the name Sami in his supplications to Allah, seeking His peace and blessings. Additionally, the name is mentioned in the Quran, where it is used to describe Allah Himself as the All-Hearing and All-Knowing (Al-Sami' Al-'Alim). This denotes the idea that Allah is always present and aware of every aspect of our lives, providing comfort and solace to believers in their struggles and trials. Therefore, bearing the name Sami is considered a reminder of Allah's presence and endless mercy, and a call to strive for inner peace and tranquility in accordance with Islamic teachings.
